readers.summary:
Read-only survey of the analysis machinery that could classify GPU helper call sites at load time (dev 52126f33; PREVAIL submodule fd85b8a6; llvmbpf submodule 87bac39a, whose line numbers below are before the parent's patch overlay; upstream PR #624 head 7aca4027 = official/codex/gpu-simt-verifier-clean; branch official/revision/automatic-warp-execution).

(1) PREVAIL never runs on CUDA probes in dev. Three things block it: it is compiled out (ENABLE_EBPF_VERIFIER defaults to OFF and is OFF in all local build trees); BPF_PROG_LOAD verifies only TRACEPOINT/SOCKET_FILTER programs; and bpftime's platform accepts only uprobe/uretprobe/tracepoint sections and HASH/ARRAY/RINGBUF maps. The wrapper API returns only optional<string>. PREVAIL computes per-instruction pre/post invariants: register type, value intervals, map_fd for map registers, and stack cells. It throws those away, keeps no map identity on lookup results, has no liveness analysis, and rejects fetch atomics, BPF-to-BPF calls and global data.

(2) Upstream's SIMT verifier (PR #624, OPEN) runs in the agent at link instantiation (nv_attach_impl::create_attach_with_ebpf_callback). It runs PREVAIL on a shadow program, then a forward worklist uniformity analysis over raw eBPF (per-pc UniformityState: regs/pointers/map_fds/stack_bytes/stack_pointer_slots), then a SIMT check. Uniformity starts from a helper table: 505, 509 and 511 are VARYING; 503, 504, 508, 510, 14 and 502 are UNIFORM; a lookup inherits its key's uniformity. It can answer "is the key at this call warp-uniform" through query_pointer_uniformity(states[pc], 2, key_size). It has no constant lattice and no control-dependence. Its soundness relies on the SIMT check rejecting lane-varying branches. Only a string escapes it. On the automatic-warp-execution branch it feeds a per-program yes/no flag, not a per-site decision. Upstream's own x86 timing: uniformity about 2 ms, PREVAIL 0.6 to 1.9 s for 4,096 instructions.

(3) llvmbpf lowers each helper call to `call i64 @_bpf_helper_ext_NNNN(i64 x5)` (no attributes; map fd as an immediate because the PTX path sets no map_by_fd). It lowers BPF_ATOMIC to monotonic atomicrmw/cmpxchg on generic pointers and registers to allocas. generate_ptx runs optimizeModule and then NVPTX codegen with no hook. The precedent hook point is do_jit_compile's inline_array_map_lookup_helpers, which runs between two optimizeModule calls. The PTX pass request carries no map information, and IR carries no eBPF pc. The local CUDA build uses LLVM 15 (legacy pass manager; no UniformityAnalysis). Kept dev PTX shows a constant fd, a literal key stored into an escaped .local slot, the null check and the dereference.

(4) Best fit per need:
- (a) result use: LLVM use-def, if the decision and the rewrite both happen in generate_ptx. Otherwise a new bytecode def-use, which does not exist today.
- (b) commutative atomic add: bytecode opcode/imm plus PR 624 pointer provenance, or LLVM atomicrmw.
- (c) uniform vs varying: only PR 624, with caveats. Literal constant: nothing ready. PREVAIL stack cells or LLVM memory analysis could recover it (inferred).
- (d) counter idiom as one unit: a bytecode pattern on PR 624-style per-pc state, or LLVM with MemorySSA (inferred); PREVAIL is a poor fit.
- (e) maps touched: PR 624 map_fds[1] or PREVAIL r1.map_fd per site, with map types from the agent's MapBasicInfo. Whether the CPU reads a map is not derivable from the program.

The call-site survey's "constant" keys are mostly pid derived from helper 14 (21 of 26 host-call sites), not literals (3).

answers.question: 1a. How does bpftime invoke the PREVAIL verifier (where, which process, which program types; is it used for CUDA probes)?
answers.answer:
Only in the syscall server, i.e. the loader process running with libbpftime-syscall-server, in the BPF_PROG_LOAD case of runtime/syscall-server/syscall_context.cpp:680-757. The verifier block (702-746) exists only when the code is compiled with ENABLE_BPFTIME_VERIFIER. That needs the CMake option ENABLE_EBPF_VERIFIER, which defaults to OFF (cmake/StandardSettings.cmake:105; wiring in runtime/CMakeLists.txt:213-217 and runtime/syscall-server/CMakeLists.txt:56-60). It is OFF in the local build trees build-cuda, build-jetson-daily and build-probecheck (their CMakeCache.txt; local build state, not part of 52126f33).

Even when compiled in, it verifies only prog_type TRACEPOINT (passed as section "tracepoint") and SOCKET_FILTER (passed as "uprobe") (syscall_context.cpp:695-701, 706). The mode comes from runtime config verifier_mode, BPFTIME_VERIFIER_LEVEL STRICT/WARNING/NO_VERIFY (703-744).

CUDA probes use SEC("kprobe/<kernel>") or SEC("kretprobe/<kernel>"). libbpf's section table maps these to BPF_PROG_TYPE_KPROBE (third_party/bpftool/libbpf/src/libbpf.c:9831, 9834). That is read from the table, not observed at a load (inferred). So CUDA probes are never verified. They would also be refused by bpftime's PREVAIL platform:
- Program types are uprobe/uretprobe/tracepoint only; anything else throws "Unsupported section by bpftime" (bpftime-verifier/src/platform-impl.cpp:18-29).
- Map types are HASH/ARRAY/RINGBUF only, so GPU map types 15xx throw (68-80).
- The usable helper set is built from the kernel-utils, shm-maps and ufunc groups (runtime/syscall-server/syscall_server_utils.cpp:189-223) and has no GPU helpers 501-511.

Map descriptors are pushed into the verifier's thread-local table at map creation (runtime/src/bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1234-1245; thread-local per bpftime-verifier/README.md:76). The agent, which compiles CUDA probes to PTX, never calls the verifier in dev. CUDA programs are recognised by name (prefix "cuda__", runtime/include/bpftime_prog.hpp:90-93).

API used: bpftime::verifier::verify_ebpf_program(const uint64_t*, size_t, const std::string &section) returns std::optional<std::string>, plus set_available_helpers, set_non_kernel_helpers and set_map_descriptors (bpftime-verifier/include/bpftime-verifier.hpp:14-68). The implementation (bpftime-verifier/src/bpftime-verifier.cpp:64-103) builds a raw_program, unmarshals it and calls PREVAIL's ebpf_verify_program, which returns only a bool. Options are at 19-30: print_invariants=true, no_simplify=true, check_termination=true.

answers.question: 1b. What per-instruction information can PREVAIL (fd85b8a6) expose: register types, map fd for pointer-to-map-value registers, value ranges, liveness?
answers.answer:
PREVAIL runs a forward abstract interpretation. crab::run_forward_analyzer(cfg, entry_dom, check_termination) returns a pair of invariant_table_t = std::map<label_t, ebpf_domain_t> holding pre and post invariants (src/crab/fwd_analyzer.hpp:14-17; called in src/crab_verifier.cpp:172-191). bpftime sets no_simplify=true, so every instruction is its own basic block and the tables are effectively per instruction.

What the domain tracks, per register and per stack cell (data_kind_t in src/crab/variable.hpp:23):
- type: T_UNINIT, T_MAP_PROGRAMS, T_MAP, T_NUM, T_CTX, T_PACKET, T_STACK, T_SHARED (src/string_constraints.hpp:17-25);
- svalue and uvalue: intervals plus relational split-DBM constraints;
- ctx/packet/shared/stack offsets;
- map_fd, for T_MAP registers produced by LDDW pseudo-map-fd (do_load_mapfd, src/crab/ebpf_domain.cpp:2179-2190);
- shared_region_size and stack_numeric_size.
Stack cells hold the same kinds, including map_fds through spills (ebpf_domain.cpp:1974).

After a map lookup, R0 becomes T_SHARED, maybe-null, shared_offset 0, shared_region_size = value_size. The pointer keeps no map fd and no call-site identity (ebpf_domain.cpp:2145-2164). Helper key and value memory contents are "not tracked" (2100).

Other limits:
- The LockAdd transfer function is empty (2083-2085).
- Unmarshal accepts only XADD with imm 0: any fetch, xchg or cmpxchg atomic throws "Unsupported atomic instruction" (src/asm_unmarshal.cpp:217-232).
- A call instruction is always treated as a helper id, so BPF-to-BPF calls fail "invalid helper function id" (asm_unmarshal.cpp:354-359). There is no local-call instruction in the Instruction variant (src/asm_syntax.hpp:312).
- LDDW with src>1 (global data) is rejected (asm_unmarshal.cpp:261).
- There is no liveness or def-use analysis. A grep finds only reverse-CFG view types meant for backward analysis (src/crab/cfg.hpp:137,400) and no backward pass.

Access: ebpf_domain_t's public API is the lattice operations, transfer functions, setup_entry, from_constraints and to_set(), which returns textual constraints (src/crab/ebpf_domain.hpp:25-80). The typed queries (get_map_type, get_map_key_size and so on) are private (81, 154-158). bpftime discards the tables: ebpf_verify_program returns a bool (crab_verifier.cpp:238-257). The printed invariants reach bpftime only inside the failure string (bpftime-verifier.cpp:96-102).

Inferred, not tested: a literal key stored on the stack should appear in the pre-invariant at the call as a stack-cell svalue, recoverable by parsing to_set() or by patching the getters public.

Cost: upstream measured PREVAIL at 1.9 s on a 4,096-instruction linear program and 0.58 s on a branchy one, against 2.2-2.5 ms for the uniformity pass. These are x86 numbers, not ours (official/revision/automatic-warp-execution:bpftime-verifier/test/device-verifier-phase-attribution-20260904.md).

answers.question: 2b. Can the SIMT verifier tell whether a helper's key argument is warp-uniform or lane-varying (from thread-index helpers 503/505/510/511)?
answers.answer:
Yes, per call site, as a three-valued answer. At a call pc, query_pointer_uniformity(states[pc], 2, key_size) joins the uniformity of the key's stack bytes when r2 is a STACK pointer with a constant, uniform offset (uniformity_analysis.cpp:711-741). key_size comes from the map descriptor of map_fds[1], or else the contiguous known stack width (373-385). This is exactly what the lookup return rule (418-429) and the SIMT key check (simt_safety_check.cpp:118-134, 257-266) use.

How the survey's key shapes would come out (inferred from the code, not run):
- block_idx out-params (503) give UNIFORM.
- warp_id (510) gives UNIFORM.
- thread_idx (505) and lane_id (511) give VARYING.
- pid from helper 14 >> 32 gives UNIFORM, since ALU-immediate ops keep uniformity (488-490). cuda-counter's call_count key is exactly that (example/gpu/cuda-counter/.output/cuda_probe.bpf.o: pc 0-2 `call 14; r0 >>= 32; *(u32*)(r10-4) = r0`, then pc 22-26 `r2 = r10-4; ... call 1`).

Limits, all read in the code:
(i) There is no constant lattice; only pointers carry constant offsets. It cannot say "literal key".
(ii) There is no control dependence: merge_state joins element-wise (267-304). A value set to different uniform constants on the two sides of a lane-varying branch merges as UNIFORM. Soundness rests on the SIMT check rejecting any lane-varying branch predicate (simt_safety_check.cpp:204-215). Per PR #624's body, kernel_trace, cudagraph, directly_run and CUTLASS run in WARNING mode because they branch on lane-varying values. In WARNING mode, uniformity values after such joins would be unreliable (inferred).
(iii) Every 0x85 call is treated as a helper (is_call, 44-47). A BPF-to-BPF call or a helper missing from the table makes get_gpu_helper_effects throw (gpu_platform.cpp:288-295), and verification fails.
(iv) A map fd spilled to the stack is lost: LDX resets map_fds (561), and STX keeps only pointer provenance (537-541). The key width then falls back to inference.
(v) STRICT mode rejects every map call with a non-uniform key (simt_safety_check.cpp:257-266), so per-thread-keyed sites cannot be classified under STRICT without separating the analysis from the rejection.
(vi) 509 (sm_id) is marked VARYING, although it should be uniform within a warp (conservative).
(vii) It says nothing about which lanes are active at the call.

answers.question: 3a. llvmbpf PTX path: where generate_ptx runs, its pass pipeline, and where an analysis/transformation could be added; is there a hook today?
answers.answer:
Call chain: the agent loads PTX pass shared libraries with dlopen and dlsym(process_input) (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:575-625). nv_attach_impl::hack_fatbin runs them per (hook entry, kernel) in a thread pool (962-1063). The RuntimeRequest carries only full_ptx, to_patch_kernel, the map_info/constData symbol names and the eBPF instruction words (pass/ptxpass_core/include/ptxpass/core.hpp:71-129). It carries no map types, sizes or analysis results. The JSON request is SHA-256-hashed into a patch cache (nv_attach_impl.cpp:994-1026). The instructions are prog->get_insns(), the stored program (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:633-644; runtime/include/bpftime_prog.hpp:65-68).

Each pass calls ptxpass::compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words (pass/ptxpass_core/src/core.cpp:226-274) with target "sm_61" (ptxpass_kprobe_entry/main.cpp:53-55, ptxpass_kretprobe/main.cpp:42-43, ptxpass_kprobe_memcapture/main.cpp:140-141). That function:
- creates a fresh llvmbpf_vm and registers dummy helpers 1, 2, 3, 6, 14, 25, 501-505 and 507-511 (506 is not registered) (234-253);
- runs load_code and llvm_bpf_jit_context::generate_ptx (255-265);
- strips the extern declarations of _bpf_helper_ext_NNNN, adds the register guard and the probe gate (267-273, 275-316).
The helper bodies come from the trampoline PTX (default_trampoline.cu).

generate_ptx (vm/llvm-jit/src/llvm_jit_context.cpp:902-972, llvmbpf 87bac39a) creates an nvptx64 TargetMachine (882-901) and calls generateModule(..., patch_map_val_at_compile_time=true, ..., is_gpu=true) (934-936). It then runs optimizeModule (default level 3, llvmbpf.hpp:157) and goes straight to legacy codegen with addPassesToEmitFile (945-971). There is no hook between them.

optimizeModule (206-290) builds PassBuilder(nullptr TM, ...) for LLVM >= 17 (247), so no target TTI. For older LLVM it uses legacy PassManagerBuilder with OptLevel, and disabled_passes/log_passes are ignored there (279-289). The local CUDA build uses LLVM 15 (build-cuda/CMakeCache.txt:689 LLVM_DIR=/usr/lib/llvm-15; llvmbpf_vm flags.make; local build state), so the legacy branch is the one in use. LLVM 15 ships LegacyDivergenceAnalysis/DivergenceAnalysis, MemorySSA and CaptureTracking headers. UniformityAnalysis.h is present only under /usr/include/llvm-16.

The public llvmbpf API has no IR callback (vm/llvm-jit/include/llvmbpf.hpp:55-166; only set_disabled_passes and set_log_passes, 108-110). ptxpass_core includes the internal llvm_jit_context.hpp.

Precedent hook: do_jit_compile (CPU JIT) runs optimizeModule, then inline_array_map_lookup_helpers(M), then optimizeModule again (515-549). inline_array_map_lookup_helpers (380-477) walks every CallInst to _bpf_helper_ext_0001, requires a ConstantInt map handle in arg 0, and rewrites per call site. The same slot in generate_ptx would be between lines 947 and 950.

The parent's overlay mechanism already replaces llvm_jit_context.cpp and compiler.cpp in the llvmbpf_vm target with patched copies (vm/compat/llvm-vm/CMakeLists.txt:16-73). ptxpass_core links llvmbpf_vm (pass/ptxpass_core/CMakeLists.txt:4), so overlay patches reach the PTX path. Local evidence: build-cuda's llvmbpf_vm objects are compiled from compiler_local_call.cpp and llvm_jit_context_array_inline.cpp, and the patched generate_ptx (build-cuda/vm/compat/llvm-vm/llvm_jit_context_array_inline.cpp:1132-1185) is unchanged. Probe PTX kept on 2026-11-10 has __local_depot0[592], the one-frame stack from local-call-return-block.patch (636501ff), alongside [16464] dumps, presumably from official builds (local /tmp state). array-map-inline.patch changes only the CPU and AOT paths.

answers.question: 3b. How does llvmbpf lower helper calls and BPF_ATOMIC instructions for NVPTX?
answers.answer:
Registers r0-r10 are i64 allocas (vm/llvm-jit/src/compiler.cpp:376-380, llvmbpf 87bac39a pre-overlay). On the GPU the BPF stack is an alloca of [N x i64] (396-402); the overlay makes it one 512-byte frame when there are no local calls (local-call-return-block.patch). Pointers are loaded from register slots as opaque ptr in address space 0 (generic).

Helpers: each registered id becomes an external declaration `i64 _bpf_helper_ext_NNNN(i64,i64,i64,i64,i64)` with no attributes: not readnone, not convergent (compiler.cpp:263-277; name from compiler_utils.hpp:39-44). emitExtFuncCall loads r1-r5, creates the call and stores the result to r0 (compiler_utils.cpp:312-371). An unregistered id is an error, "Ext func not found" (366-369).

Maps: with map_by_fd unset, as in the PTX path where core.cpp never calls set_lddw_helpers, LDDW src=1 stores the raw fd imm as an i64 constant (compiler.cpp:1111-1127). The map argument therefore reaches the call as a constant fd, and the trampoline indexes __constant__ map_info[fd] to pick the path at run time (attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline/default_trampoline.cu:84-101, 233-285). LDDW src=2 (global data) requires map_val because generate_ptx passes patch_map_val_at_compile_time=true. The PTX path has no map_val, so compilation fails (1156-1166).

Local calls: BPF-to-BPF calls use an in-memory call stack plus indirectbr over block addresses inside one function (426-448, 509-560, 1420-1468).

Atomics: ADD, AND, OR and XOR, with or without FETCH, become atomicrmw on gep(i8, ptr reg, off), Monotonic ordering, align 4/8; FETCH stores the old value into src (compiler.cpp:1637-1681; compiler_utils.cpp:372-401). XCHG becomes atomicrmw xchg (1682-1689). CMPXCHG emits a plain load and a cmpxchg, and stores the plain load (not the cmpxchg result) into r0 (1690-1719). verifyModule is skipped for the GPU (1751). The only pc link is the block name bb_inst_<pc> at block starts (470-477). DILocations are added only if BTF line info was loaded (562-623), and the PTX path never loads it.

Observed PTX (dev build, local /tmp/bpftime-fatbin-work.C6s4z5/patched.temp.1.sm_75.ptx:2123-2211, 2026-11-10), whose shape matches benchmark/gpu/micro/cuda_probe.bpf.c:211-219:
- `st.local.u32 [%rd1+508], 0` (literal key into an escaped stack slot);
- `call.uni (retval0), _bpf_helper_ext_0001` with param0 = 16 (map fd) and param1 = the slot address;
- `setp.eq.s64 %p1, %rd10, 0; @%p1 bra`;
- generic `ld.u32 [%rd10]` / `[%rd10+4]`, `add 1`, then `_bpf_helper_ext_0002(16, slot, value slot, 0)`.
Also results/gpu/examples-20261109/ptx/kernel_trace-sample.patched.ptx:1814-1960 passes the constant fd 3 to _bpf_helper_ext_0025.

answers.question: 3c. Can standard LLVM analyses (use-def of the call result, liveness, recognising atomicrmw add on the pointer returned by a lookup, constant keys) be applied after lifting?
answers.answer:
Partly. The answer rests on code reading plus the observed PTX; no IR dump exists.
- Use-def: after optimizeModule (mem2reg/SROA in O3), the i64 result of `_bpf_helper_ext_0001` should have direct users (inferred): none, an icmp with 0, inttoptr then gep then load/store/atomicrmw, or an argument of another helper call. The observed dev PTX shows the null check and the dereference surviving O3 as straight-line uses. Use-def before optimizeModule is useless because every register goes through allocas (compiler.cpp:376-380).
- atomicrmw add: emitted directly from BPF_ATOMIC ADD (compiler.cpp:1640-1648). Tracing its pointer operand back to inttoptr(call result) plus a constant gep should be mechanical (inferred).
- Constant keys: the key argument is ptrtoint of a slot in the BPF stack alloca. That stack escapes into every helper call, which carries no attributes, so the literal is not forwarded into the call. The observed PTX keeps `st.local.u32 [slot], 0` before the call. Recovering it needs a memory query, e.g. MemorySSA's clobbering store for that slot; available in LLVM 15 (inferred approach).
- Map identity: arg0 is a ConstantInt fd (observed). Map type or size is not available in the pass.
- Uniformity: LLVM 15 (the local build) has only (Legacy)DivergenceAnalysis; UniformityAnalysis starts in LLVM 16. Lane variance here comes from opaque helper calls (505, 511) writing to escaped stack memory, and optimizeModule builds PassBuilder with a null TargetMachine (llvm_jit_context.cpp:247). LLVM's own divergence analyses would need a helper-id-aware divergence source (inferred; NVPTX TTI behaviour not read in this tree).
- Caveats: IR call sites carry no eBPF pc (compiler.cpp:562-623), so combining with a bytecode-level analysis needs new metadata. O3 may merge or duplicate helper call sites, for example sinking two printk calls (inferred, unverified). BPF-to-BPF calls go through an in-memory call stack and indirectbr (509-560), which breaks register use-def across local calls. The probe is compiled for sm_61, which limits any warp intrinsics inserted at IR level (inferred; activemask and vote.sync need sm_70+).

answers.question: 4a. Need: is the result of a call used (null check only vs dereference vs passed on)? Which machinery fits best?
answers.answer:
Discriminating constraints:
- A def-use or liveness relation from the call's R0 is needed, including copies, stack spills and the null branch.
- The decision must map back to the call site that gets rewritten.

Options:
- PREVAIL: no. It has no liveness or def-use, only forward invariants (src/crab/cfg.hpp has reverse views but no backward pass). The lookup pointer keeps no call identity (ebpf_domain.cpp:2145-2164).
- PR #624 uniformity: partial. PointerProvenance marks MAP_VALUE pointers and follows them through mov and 8-byte stack spills (uniformity_analysis.cpp:461-465, 537-541, 585-591). It records neither the producing call nor any uses.
- dev's bytecode reachability analysis (runtime/src/bpftime_prog_reachability.cpp, 0d5b37af) gives a worklist and CFG skeleton with BPF-to-BPF call handling (263-271), but it tracks registers only and records no uses.
- LLVM IR after optimizeModule: the most direct, via users of the CallInst (inferred). Observed dev PTX shows `setp.eq` with 0 plus generic loads from the result (local /tmp dump), and cuda-counter's retprobe passes the lookup pointer as update's value (r3 = r0, cuda_probe.bpf.o retprobe pc 40). Its constraints: no eBPF pc on IR (compiler.cpp:562-623), no map info in the pass request (core.hpp:71-129), and the transformation would have to happen in the same place (between llvm_jit_context.cpp:947 and 950).

Fit: LLVM, if decision and rewrite both live in generate_ptx. If the decision must be taken in the agent before the PTX pass (where map types are known), a small new bytecode def-use pass is needed; nothing existing provides it.

answers.question: 4b. Need: is the operation through a returned pointer a commutative atomic add?
answers.answer:
Bytecode form: STX|ATOMIC (opcode 0xdb for 64-bit, 0xc3 for 32-bit) with imm 0x00 (ADD) or 0x01 (ADD|FETCH, old value into src). cuda-counter pc 28 is `db 60 00 00 00 00 00 00` = `lock *(u64*)(r0+0) += r6`, i.e. no FETCH, and r0 is the lookup result after `if r0 == 0 goto +2` (local cuda_probe.bpf.o; source example/gpu/cuda-counter/cuda_probe.bpf.c:48-50 uses __atomic_add_fetch with the result unused).

Options:
- PR #624: already recognises atomics (is_atomic, uniformity_analysis.cpp:49-53) and knows the base register's provenance: region MAP_VALUE plus constant_offset (uniformity_analysis.hpp:31-39). An atomic ADD on a MAP_VALUE pointer at constant offset is decidable at the bytecode level. Which lookup produced the pointer is not recorded.
- LLVM: atomicrmw add, Monotonic, generic pointer (compiler.cpp:1640-1648; compiler_utils.cpp:376-388), so the opcode is explicit. Provenance means tracing inttoptr back to the helper call (inferred).
- PREVAIL: unfit. Fetch, xchg and cmpxchg are unmarshal errors (asm_unmarshal.cpp:217-232), and LockAdd is a no-op (ebpf_domain.cpp:2083-2085).

The non-atomic forms are a plain load, add and store: `*total += delta` in cuda-counter's retprobe at pc 33-35, followed by update(BPF_EXIST, value = the lookup pointer) at pc 40-41; `newv = *val + 1; update(BPF_ANY)` in benchmark/gpu/micro/cuda_probe.bpf.c:211-219. Treating them as commutative is a semantic choice. None of the machinery marks them; upstream's eligibility even admits the plain store (simt_safety_check.cpp:223-229 with warp_execution_eligibility.cpp:141-156).

Note: llvmbpf's CMPXCHG lowering stores a plain pre-load into r0, not the cmpxchg result (compiler.cpp:1690-1719).

answers.question: 4c. Need: is the key constant, warp-uniform, or lane-varying?
4d. Need: recognise the multi-instruction counter idiom (lookup, null branch to update NOEXIST, atomic add) as one unit.
4e. Need: which maps a program touches and with which helpers.
answers.answer:
Per call site (helper id, map fd):
- PR #624: state.map_fds[1] at the call pc (uniformity_analysis.cpp:444-451, 461-465). Lost if the fd is spilled to the stack (561).
- PREVAIL: r1.map_fd in the pre-invariant, tracked through stack spills (ebpf_domain.cpp:1974), but readable only via to_set() or private getters.
- LLVM: arg0 ConstantInt (compiler.cpp:1111-1127; observed fd 16 and fd 3 in PTX).

Whole-program scans already in dev, both linear and not per call site:
- typed_helper_map_type (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:101-177): LDDW pseudo-map fds plus whether a helper id occurs;
- bind_array_maps (runtime/src/bpftime_prog.cpp:238-330; CUDA excluded at 246).

Map metadata: the agent builds an fd-indexed MapBasicInfo[1024] (enabled, key/value size, max_entries, map_type, extra_buffer, max_thread_count) from handler_manager (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:505-554). It goes to nv_attach_private_data (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:643-644) and to the device as __constant__ map_info (default_trampoline.cu:84-101). It is not passed to the PTX pass (core.hpp:71-129).

Not derivable from any program analysis: whether the CPU side reads or writes a map. This is what separates eliminate from defer. It needs a runtime view: other programs in handler_manager referencing the fd, and the loader's bpf() map commands, which reach the syscall server (syscall_context.cpp BPF_MAP_* cases). The call-site survey established this by reading loaders by hand (callsite-survey README).

facts.statement: ENABLE_EBPF_VERIFIER defaults to OFF; PREVAIL is compiled into the runtime and syscall server only when it is ON.
All three local build trees (build-cuda, build-jetson-daily, build-probecheck) have ENABLE_EBPF_VERIFIER=OFF (local build state).
bpftime runs PREVAIL only at BPF_PROG_LOAD in the syscall server, and only for prog_type TRACEPOINT (section "tracepoint") or SOCKET_FILTER (section "uprobe").
bpftime's PREVAIL platform accepts only uprobe/uretprobe/tracepoint sections and HASH/ARRAY/RINGBUF maps; other sections and map types (all 15xx GPU maps) throw.
verify_ebpf_program returns std::optional<std::string> and calls PREVAIL's ebpf_verify_program, which returns bool; invariants are not returned.
After bpf_map_lookup_elem, PREVAIL types R0 as T_SHARED with shared_offset 0 and shared_region_size = value_size; no map fd is kept for the value pointer.
PREVAIL fd85b8a6 rejects atomic instructions with imm != 0 (fetch, xchg, cmpxchg), treats every call as a helper call (no BPF-to-BPF calls), and rejects LDDW with src > 1.
PREVAIL's typed map getters on ebpf_domain_t are private; the public read-out is to_set() (string constraints).
PR #624 (GPU SIMT verifier) is OPEN, head 7aca4027 (local ref official/codex/gpu-simt-verifier-clean), 22 files +3086/-20, last updated 2026-11-12.
PR #624's uniformity_analysis, simt_safety_check and gpu_platform files are byte-identical on official/revision/automatic-warp-execution; that branch's gpu_verifier.cpp only adds phase timing.
facts.source: git show of both refs; diff of the two gpu_verifier.cpp copies

facts.statement: The GPU verifier runs in the agent inside nv_attach_impl::create_attach_with_ebpf_callback, using map descriptors built from MapBasicInfo; STRICT mode returns GPU_VERIFIER_REJECTED (-4096).

The uniformity analysis is a forward worklist over raw eBPF that stores an input UniformityState per pc (regs, PointerProvenance, map_fds, 512 stack bytes, stack pointer slots) with an element-wise join.
GPU helper uniformity table: VARYING for 2, 3, 6, 25, 505, 509, 511; UNIFORM for 1 (lookup result follows key uniformity), 14, 501, 502, 503, 504, 506, 507, 508, 510.

The SIMT check rejects lane-varying branch predicates, non-uniform atomic addresses, lane-varying shared map stores, prohibited helpers 501/506, and non-uniform map keys, update values and printk arguments.

Upstream's automatic warp execution makes a yes/no decision per program: any atomic, helpers 25/6/501/507, or update/delete on a map that is not a shared GPU map (1501/1503/1504/1513) makes the program ineligible.
Upstream timing on 4,096-instruction synthetic programs (x86): PREVAIL 1,907 ms and 584 ms against uniformity 2.2 ms and 2.5 ms and SIMT 0.01 ms and 0.03 ms.
ptxpass compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words registers dummy helpers 1, 2, 3, 6, 14, 25, 501-505 and 507-511 (not 506) and calls llvm_bpf_jit_context::generate_ptx; the passes use target "sm_61".
The PTX pass RuntimeRequest carries only the PTX, the kernel name, symbol names and the eBPF words; there is no map info.
PTX passes are dlopen'ed libraries run in the agent per (hook entry, kernel) in a thread pool, with a patch cache keyed by the SHA-256 of the request JSON.
generate_ptx runs optimizeModule and then NVPTX codegen with no hook in between; the CPU JIT path runs optimizeModule, inline_array_map_lookup_helpers, then optimizeModule again.
inline_array_map_lookup_helpers is an existing per-call-site IR transformation: it walks CallInsts to _bpf_helper_ext_0001 with a ConstantInt map handle and rewrites them.
The llvmbpf public API has no IR or pass callback, only set_disabled_passes and set_log_passes.

The local CUDA build uses LLVM 15, so optimizeModule takes the legacy PassManagerBuilder branch, where disabled_passes and log_passes are ignored; UniformityAnalysis.h exists only under llvm-16 locally.
The parent's llvmbpf overlay replaces llvm_jit_context.cpp and compiler.cpp in the llvmbpf_vm target, which ptxpass_core links, so overlay patches reach the PTX path.
Helper calls lower to `call i64 @_bpf_helper_ext_NNNN(i64 x5)` declarations without attributes; the result is stored to the r0 alloca.
With map_by_fd unset (the PTX path), LDDW pseudo-map-fd becomes the raw fd as an i64 constant; global-data LDDW (src=2) fails because generate_ptx requires map_val.
BPF_ATOMIC ADD/AND/OR/XOR (with or without FETCH) and XCHG lower to Monotonic atomicrmw on a generic pointer; CMPXCHG stores a plain pre-load into r0 instead of the cmpxchg result.
llvmbpf IR carries no eBPF pc: DILocations only when BTF line info is loaded (the PTX path does not load it), and bb_inst_<pc> names only at block starts.

Observed dev probe PTX: a literal key stored to a .local slot, call.uni _bpf_helper_ext_0001 with map fd 16 as a constant parameter, setp.eq null check, generic loads from the result, then _bpf_helper_ext_0002 with flags 0.

cuda-counter's counter idiom in bytecode: call 1 at pc 26, `if r0 == 0 goto +2`, `lock *(u64*)(r0+0) += r6` (imm 0, no fetch), else update with r4 = 1 (BPF_NOEXIST) on the same key slot r10-4; the key is pid from call 14 >> 32.
Of 26 survey host-call sites with key_scope "constant", 21 use &pid (helper 14), 3 use a literal key 0, and 2 are printk without a key.

dev already has a bytecode forward analysis (constant propagation and reachability over registers, no stack modelling) used at load time to retarget unreachable missing-helper calls; it lives in the CPU-side load path, while the nv attach path reads the stored instructions.

The agent builds an fd-indexed MapBasicInfo[1024] (type, key/value size, max_entries, extra_buffer, max_thread_count) for CUDA attach; the trampoline dispatches each map helper on map_info[fd].map_type at run time.

open_questions: Where should the per-site decision run? In the agent before the PTX pass (has MapBasicInfo, works on bytecode, no LLVM), or inside generate_ptx (has LLVM use-def, but no map info and no eBPF pc)? A split design needs map info in RuntimeRequest (which then becomes part of the patch-cache key) and pc metadata on helper CallInsts (none emitted today).

Can PR #624's analyze_uniformity be lifted into dev without enabling ENABLE_EBPF_VERIFIER and PREVAIL? It does not call PREVAIL but includes PREVAIL headers via gpu_platform.hpp, and dev builds have the option OFF.

Uniformity has no control dependence. Should per-site aggregation require warp-uniform branches (as PR #624's SIMT check does), or should a divergence-aware join be added? Most leader-pattern examples branch on thread index (PR #624 runs them in WARNING mode).
Fold helper 14 (pid) to a constant at PTX generation time? The agent knows the pid, and 21 of the survey's 26 'constant' host-call keys are pid.
Does LLVM 15 O3 (legacy pipeline) merge or duplicate helper call sites, e.g. sink the two printk calls in cuda-counter's retprobe? No IR dump exists, and log_passes is ignored on the LLVM 15 branch.

Probes are compiled with target sm_61 while the device compile uses the detected arch. IR-level warp intrinsics (activemask, vote.sync, match.any) need sm_70+ PTX. Does aggregation have to be emitted at PTX text level, as upstream's leader prefix is?

Non-atomic read-modify-write through a lookup pointer (cuda-counter retprobe, cuda_probe micro, cudagraph): treat it as a commutative accumulate (defer/aggregate) or keep it synchronous? Per-thread execution of it is already racy.
Which component should know whether the CPU side reads a map (eliminate vs defer)? No program analysis can; it needs handler_manager plus syscall-server knowledge of the loader's bpf() map commands.
Should llvmbpf's CMPXCHG lowering (r0 gets a plain pre-load) be fixed before any analysis relies on cmpxchg semantics?
The PREVAIL pin fd85b8a6 (2023-09) lacks BPF-to-BPF calls, fetch atomics and global data. Bump it, or avoid PREVAIL for GPU probes?

verdicts.item: (a) Where per-call-site decisions could be computed, and how they would reach PTX generation (compile-path reader)
verdicts.detail:
Read at 52126f33.

The agent is the first place where the instructions, map metadata and the attach point are all together. The CUDA link branch of bpf_attach_ctx.cpp sets nv_attach_private_data.instructions = prog->get_insns() (the stored originals, line 639) and map_basic_info = create_map_basic_info(1024) (643-644), then calls create_attach_with_ebpf_callback (645-648).

create_attach_with_ebpf_callback (nv_attach_impl.cpp:181-285):
- copies the instructions into nv_attach_entry (220) and stores it in hook_entries[id] (232);
- sets this->map_basic_info = data.map_basic_info (233). This happens once per link, and the last link wins.

nv_attach_entry already has two unused carrier fields, parameters and extras (nv_attach_impl.hpp:76-88).

From there the route to the compiler is:
- hack_fatbin builds a RuntimeRequest per (PTX file × entry × kernel) (994-1005). It looks it up in patch_cache by the sha256 of the request JSON (1019) and otherwise calls the pass's process_input (1059).
- The pass calls compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words(words, "sm_61", ...) (kprobe_entry main.cpp:53-55).
- That function registers fixed helpers on a fresh llvmbpf_vm (core.cpp:234-253) and calls generate_ptx.
- generate_ptx (llvm_jit_context.cpp:903-975 at llvmbpf 87bac39a, pre-overlay) runs generateModule, one optimizeModule, then NVPTX codegen, with no hook in between.

The overlay does not touch generate_ptx:
- array-map-inline.patch's last hunk is @@ -790 (the function is at 903).
- The overlay copy in the local build (build-cuda/vm/compat/llvm-vm/llvm_jit_context_array_inline.cpp:1132ff, 11-10 build) is byte-identical to the submodule's in that function.
- llvm_jit_context.cpp is already an overlaid TU (vm/compat/llvm-vm/CMakeLists.txt:20-44), so a GPU hook would be one more hunk in an existing patch.

Refinements to the reader:
(1) RuntimeRequest is {input: RuntimeInput, ebpf_instructions} (core.hpp:111-129).
- Only RuntimeInput uses NLOHMANN_DEFINE_TYPE_NON_INTRUSIVE_WITH_DEFAULT (core.hpp:77), so a new field is backward-compatible only inside `input`.
- RuntimeRequest itself uses plain NON_INTRUSIVE (129).
- Upstream's automatic-warp-execution branch puts its per-program flag in RuntimeInput (core.hpp:82-92 there).
(2) The full set of GPU programs (all hook_entries) first exists together when hack_fatbin runs at module load. create_attach_with_ebpf_callback sees one link at a time.
(3) The pass's thread pool posts one task per extracted PTX file (nv_attach_impl.cpp:975). Entries × kernels run sequentially inside a task and chain on current_ptx (1109).

Inferred (not run): a decision placed in the request JSON automatically becomes part of the patch_cache key.

In dev today no GPU program is affected:
- All 22 GPU .bpf.c files define BPF_NO_GLOBAL_DATA.
- None references helper 506 (grep).

verdicts.item: (b) How a call site could get its own callee: bytecode helper-id rewrite vs llvmbpf IR pass vs PTX rewrite
verdicts.detail:
All three mechanisms read as the reader described.

Bytecode helper-id rewrite:
- Each helper id maps to one shared symbol, _bpf_helper_ext_%04d (compiler_utils.hpp:39-44).
- A new id must be registered in compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words (core.cpp:234-253), or the compile exits the application (see (a')).
- It must also be defined in the trampoline (or emitted in the same module). The filter strips only `.extern` declarations of 4-digit _bpf_helper_ext names (core.cpp:280-283).

IR pass:
- generate_ptx has no hook (see (a)).
- The overlay precedent is the direct_helpers block (array-map-inline.patch hunk @@ -383,9 +423,53).
- Nuance: that block retargets each CallInst, but chooses by constant map handle (vm.array_maps[handle].direct_helpers), so the decision is per map, not per call site. Every call on the same handle gets the same callee.
- IR carries no eBPF pc: emitExtFuncCall attaches no metadata (compiler_utils.cpp:312-370).

PTX rewrite:
- It works on text after O3, in which the fd constant is shared through a register (reader's 11-10 sample).

A fourth option the readers did not list: pass a per-site id or decision in an unused helper argument and keep the shared callee. What is free, from the trampoline signatures:
- lookup _bpf_helper_ext_0001(map,key,a,b,c): r3-r5 unused (default_trampoline.cu:233-234);
- update 0002(map,key,value,flags,a): r5 unused (287-288);
- delete 0003: r3-r5 unused (368-369);
- printk 0006 and perf_event_output 0025: all 5 used (387, 430-431);
- 0014 and 0501: no map argument.
Doing this in IR means setting a call operand, with no jump-offset fixups. Doing it in bytecode means inserting a mov before each call and fixing jumps. memcapture already inserts instructions, but only at pc 0 (memcapture main.cpp:~60-133).

Inferred: any pc-keyed decision must add memcapture's prepended instruction count. memcapture also compiles one copy of the program per captured ld/st line ("__memcapture__"+count, main.cpp:53-57, 140-147).

- BPF_MAP_LOOKUP_ELEM calls bpftime_map_lookup_elem, which passes from_syscall=true (bpftime_shm.cpp:88-92), then memcpy's from the returned pointer in the segment (syscall_context.cpp:600-624).

verdicts.item: (c2) No channel exists for the loader to make the agent flush before a read
verdicts.detail:
Read:
- The agent socket accepts only 'refresh ...', 'detach' and 'status' (agent.cpp:365-404).
- A grep of runtime/syscall-server for the agent socket name, epoch reads or CommSharedMem finds no use of the socket.
- SIGUSR1 means detach.
- epoch_seq signals sessions only.

Added by reading the watcher, inferred and not run: the watcher would take any flag1 == 1 it sees. try_serve CASes flag1 from 1 to 0 with acquire (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:303-317). When parked it rechecks at the 1 ms backstop (activity.wait_for_note, 411). So a loader that wrote flag1 would be served within about 1 ms.

But it is not a usable channel:
- Mutual exclusion on the slot is occupy_flag, taken only by GPU atomicCAS (default_trampoline.cu:146-149, unscoped atom.cas). The CPU never takes it, so a CPU poster could overwrite a GPU thread's request.
- serve_cuda_request knows only the GPU opcodes and logs anything else as 'Unknown request id' (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:184-186).
- A served request with no noted launch counts as a hit for the watcher's unseen-launch latch.
sources: git grep over runtime/syscall-server for the agent socket name, epoch_seq and CommSharedMem

verdicts.item: (d) A hash-map lookup's value pointer does not stay on its key across a concurrent update/delete of the same key in dev's hash map
verdicts.detail:
hash_map_impl is fix_size_hash_map_impl unless BPFTIME_USE_VAR_HASH_MAP is defined. `git grep -n BPFTIME_USE_VAR_HASH_MAP` finds only #ifdef uses (map_handler.cpp:61, 1097, 1834) and no definition, so fix_size is what is compiled.

What bpftime_hash_map::update does (bpftime_hash_map.hpp:715-745):
- NOEXIST on an existing key returns `exists` with no change.
- ANY or EXIST on an existing key calls replace_locked (528-538). That links the stripe's spare (holding the new key and value) in place of the old element, retires the old element (new generation, 483-488) and makes it the stripe's spare. The next existing-key update in that stripe overwrites it.

elem_delete (755-781) unlinks and retires the element under the stripe lock, then gives it to a free list.

The header comments say the same: "valid until the key is updated or deleted" (100-101), and "A value pointer from a lookup stays on the old element, which the next update in that stripe reuses" (523-524).

The address itself stays inside the segment. Nothing pins hash storage, though: a loader close calls clear_id_at, then map_free (handler_manager.cpp:116-123; syscall_context.cpp:273-296). Only ARRAY gets a GPU pin (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:480-503).

On the Orin, 1501 is created as an ordinary HASH (bpftime_shm.hpp:142-154; syscall_context.cpp:566-577), so the same rules apply to it.

verdicts.item: (e2) The suspected non-atomic += miscount under auto-warp
verdicts.detail:
Confirmed as a code-reading inference, not run.

Why `*val = *val + 1` is admitted:
- A literal key stored with ST becomes UNIFORM stack bytes (uniformity_analysis.cpp:512-524).
- The lookup returns UNIFORM r0 and a MAP_VALUE pointer with UNIFORM pointee (594-645), so the null branch is uniform.
- The LDX through it is UNIFORM, and so is +1.
- The STX of a uniform value into a shared-map value passes SIMT (simt_safety_check.cpp:223-229) and eligibility (warp_execution_eligibility.cpp:141-156); only atomics are rejected (132-134).

The lowering elects the lowest active, predicate-true lane via activemask / vote.ballot.sync (official core.cpp:403-470). The handler therefore runs once per converged group that reaches the hook.

Witness: mem_trace is not one, because it is __memcapture, which is not lowered. Concrete programs in dev's tree that satisfy every rule by reading (PREVAIL step not run):
- benchmark/gpu/micro/cuda_probe.bpf.c cuda__probe_hash_lookup (HASH, kprobe, lookup + (*val)++);
- cuda__probe_array_lookup (ARRAY);
- cuda__retprobe_gpu_array_update (1503, kretprobe, lookup + update(BPF_ANY, *val+1) with a uniform value).

Framing, which differs between readers:
- Against an exact per-thread count, this undercounts (overlap survey).
- Against dev's current per-thread execution of the same plain RMW, it is not a regression. Today's host_call serves all 32 lanes' lookups before any lane returns (default_trampoline.cu:142-171), and the converged plain store then collapses to about one update per warp. That is the #739/#740 collapse.
- Dev's mem_trace is still the non-atomic version: 466e91b0 (#740, merged upstream) is not an ancestor of 52126f33.

verdicts.item: (f2) Which hooked calls could act as flush points, and when the agent learns a probed kernel finished
verdicts.detail:
Launch hooks run on the launching thread, before and after the original launch. In substitution mode they take the original path and then call note_launch_if_probed (nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:198-207).

Kernel completion is seen only by the watcher's cuEventQuery over one CUevent per stream:
- at most every event_query_every_us (1000 us), or every 100 us with WFE (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:244-245, 334-358);
- the events come from probed_launch_activity::note.

The last detach waits only for late-path launch events (nv_attach_impl.cpp:159-170, 1521-1525).

Precision on launches that are not noted. For a CUDA 13 kernel handle, the cudaLaunchKernel replacement does fire. But note_launch_if_probed resolves the handle with cudaGetFuncBySymbol, which fails for a kernel handle (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1575-1584), so the launch is cached as not probed and never noted. CLAUDE.md:2240-2243 lists 'CUDA 13 kernel handles the hooks cannot resolve, nvcc 13's default launches when they are not resolved'.

Graph launches reach no hook at all: cudaGraphLaunch is not hooked.

So for these launches there is no completion signal, and a flush tied to kernel completion is unavailable (inferred from the code; CLAUDE.md describes the watcher answering them at the 1 ms park backstop).

contradictions: Pass loading. device-side (fact: 'dlopen ... nv_attach_impl.cpp:602-609') and analysis-tools ('dlopen and dlsym') contradict compile-path ('dlmopen LM_ID_NEWLM'). Resolved: dlmopen(LM_ID_NEWLM, path, RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL) at attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:593-594. Each pass .so therefore gets its own link-map namespace and its own static llvmbpf copy (ptxpass_core links llvmbpf_vm PUBLIC, pass/ptxpass_core/CMakeLists.txt:4).

LLVM version. compile-path cites /usr/lib/llvm-16 Error.h for ExitOnError; analysis-tools says the build uses LLVM 15. Resolved: all local build caches have LLVM_DIR=/usr/lib/llvm-15 (CMakeCache.txt:689 in candidate build-cuda, build-jetson-daily, build-probecheck and bpftime-gpu-work/policy/build-cuda). ExitOnError::checkError calls exit() in llvm-15 Error.h:1381-1385 too. So optimizeModule takes the legacy PassManagerBuilder branch, and UniformityAnalysis (LLVM 16+) is unavailable.

Warp-intrinsic target limit. analysis-tools: 'activemask, vote.sync, match.any need sm_70+ PTX', so the sm_61 probe target forbids them. device-side lists activemask in the sm_61 trampoline. Resolved:
- attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline_ptx.h is `.version 8.1 / .target sm_61` (lines 6-7) and contains activemask.b32 6 times, so LLVM/clang emit it for sm_61.
- rewrite_ptx_target replaces .target with the detected arch (sm_87 on the Orin) before nvPTXCompiler --gpu-name=<arch> (nv_attach_utils.cpp:31-67; nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:134-160).
- So the sm_61 limit binds only intrinsics lowered by LLVM's NVPTX backend in generate_ptx / clang. That plausibly covers match.sync (sm_70) and redux.sync (sm_80), per PTX ISA knowledge, not read. It does not bind PTX text or inline asm.
- Upstream's leader lowering inserts activemask/vote.ballot.sync as PTX text, gated only on .version >= 6.0 (official core.cpp:336-353).

Request slot scope. The task text and semantics (Q1h: 'one request slot per process') say per process; device-side and host-side say per segment. Resolved: CommSharedMem is one named object 'cuda_comm_shared_mem' in the Boost segment. The server constructs it and agents find it (runtime/src/bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1052-1084). Each agent zeroes it when creating its CUDA context (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:615). It is per process only when one CUDA process uses the segment; several are 'not covered' (CLAUDE.md:2318-2319).

Per-CPU maps through a GPU host call. device-side (Q1b, inferred): 'the host picks the watcher thread's CPU (my_sched_getcpu)'. host-side (Q1c): from_syscall=true takes the userspace path. Resolved for host-side:
- bpftime_map_lookup_elem passes from_syscall=true (bpftime_shm.cpp:88-92).
- bpf_map_handler routes PERCPU_ARRAY/PERCPU_HASH to do_lookup_userspace when from_syscall (map_handler.cpp:173-184).
- per_cpu_array_map_impl::elem_lookup_userspace returns data_at(key,0) (CPU 0) only when percpu_userspace_is_packed_storage holds. Otherwise it returns a static thread_local heap buffer (per_cpu_array_map.cpp:184-200; map_common_def.hpp:172-176,206-214), which the GPU cannot reach, so the result is NULL (inferred).
- my_sched_getcpu is not on this path.

Pass thread-pool granularity. analysis-tools: passes run 'per (hook entry, kernel) in a thread pool'. Resolved: hack_fatbin posts one pool task per extracted PTX file (nv_attach_impl.cpp:975). Inside it, hook entries × kernels run sequentially, and each pass consumes the previous pass's output (current_ptx = resp.output_ptx, 1109). This matches compile-path's 'per extracted PTX file × hook entry × kernel'.

Key scope of the timestamp-idiom deletes. semantics Q2-J puts D (cuda-counter, rocm-counter) under block-uniform keys. records.json marks the delete sites cuda-counter:70 and rocm-counter:71 key_scope 'constant' (&pid); only the entry update and exit lookup are per_block. analysis-tools' count (26 constant = 21 pid + 3 literal 0 + 2 printk) agrees with records.json (host-call key_scope tally: constant 26, per_block 14, none 11, per_thread 4, per_warp 4).

Precedent for per-call-site IR retargeting. compile-path calls the array-map-inline.patch direct_helpers block a precedent for per-call-site retargeting. Resolved as a nuance: it iterates CallInsts, but the choice is keyed on the constant map handle (vm.array_maps.find(handle)->direct_helpers), so all calls on one map get the same callee. It is a per-map decision applied at call granularity (array-map-inline.patch hunk @@ -383,9 +423,53 @@).

Auto-warp += 'undercount'. The overlap survey frames the leader-only result of a non-atomic `*val = *val + 1` as an undercount. semantics notes it equals today's lockstep collapse. Both hold, against different references:
- It undercounts against an exact per-thread count.
- It matches dev's current behaviour for the same plain RMW. host_call serves all lanes' lookups before any lane returns (default_trampoline.cu:142-171), and the converged plain store collapses to about one per warp.
- Upstream merged #740 (466e91b0), which makes mem_trace atomic. It is not in dev.

The host has no keyed add-or-create operation for HASH:

- bpftime_hash_map::with_existing_value (fn on the value under the key's stripe lock) exists, but its only non-test user is the per-CPU hash.

gaps_filled.fact:
Map identity on the GPU is only the fd:
- map_info has no generation field.
- A loader close() of a map fd clears the handler and frees the map (clear_id_at, then map_free) under the binding mutex.
- Only ordinary ARRAY storage is pinned for patched modules (gpu_array_bindings).
- The fd can then be reused by a new handler.
Deferred HASH work applied after a close could hit a freed or different map (inferred).

An attach that arrives after cudart already loaded the modules does not substitute. It warns and switches to the late path: patched copies, with launches redirected by kernel name. So a per-site design must work on both the substitution and the late path.

memcapture works differently from the entry pass:
- It prepends LDDW/STXDW instructions (the captured PTX line written to the stack), so eBPF pcs shift by the prepended count.
- It compiles the whole program once per captured memory-access line.
A pc-keyed decision must account for both.

There is no load-time signal that the loader reads or writes a map:
- The handler stores map flags (attr.flags) and freeze state (is_frozen), but MapBasicInfo carries neither.
- BPF_F_WRONLY/BPF_F_RDONLY are enforced only in var_hash_map, which is not compiled.
- The surveyed GPU examples use only BPF_F_MMAPABLE.
- The map usage counters exist only in counting builds (BPFTIME_ENABLE_MAP_USAGE_STATS, OFF in build-cuda), and they record GPU host calls with from_syscall=true, the same as loader bpf() calls.

gaps_filled.fact: The agent can allocate in the shared segment: it inserts its pid into a Boost interprocess set there. Every agent registers the whole fixed-size segment with cuMemHostRegister(DEVICEMAP|PORTABLE). Inferred: a GPU-side buffer the agent constructs in the segment would be both device-reachable (cuMemHostGetDevicePointer) and readable by the loader without the agent's help, as the 1527 ringbuf is today.

For CUDA 13 kernel handles the launch replacement does fire. But note_launch_if_probed's cudaGetFuncBySymbol fails, the result is cached as not probed and the launch is not noted. Graph launches reach no hook at all. Neither gives the agent a completion event.
BPF_CMPXCHG in llvmbpf sets R0 from a plain load taken before the cmpxchg and discards the cmpxchg result. A GPU CAS loop could therefore see wrong success or failure. The overlay does not touch it.

Survey host-call sites (59; tally in records.json):
- key_scope: constant 26, per_block 14, none 11, per_thread 4, per_warp 4;
- result_use: unused 45, pointer_rmw 9, value_used 5.
No host-call site uses a helper's integer return value.

I re-read the critical facts myself at dev 52126f33, upstream e27d009b/7aca4027 and llvmbpf 87bac39a (pre-overlay line numbers). Nothing was built or run. All six checked items (a–f) hold, with these refinements:

- **(a) Where per-site decisions are made.** The agent's CUDA link instantiation, and nv_attach_impl::create_attach_with_ebpf_callback, are the first places where the instructions, the fd-indexed map_info and the attach point are together. But that function sees one link at a time, and map_basic_info is last-link-wins. All GPU programs exist together only when hack_fatbin runs at module load.
- **(a) How a decision reaches the compiler.** The route is nv_attach_entry (unused `parameters`/`extras` fields), then RuntimeInput (the only backward-compatible JSON struct, and part of the patch-cache key), then compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words, then an llvmbpf setter, then generate_ptx. generate_ptx has no hook, and the overlay leaves it untouched.
- **(a') Bad helper ids exit the application.** An unregistered helper id or a map-value LDDW calls exit() through ExitOnError in generate_ptx. The build uses LLVM 15, not 16.
- **(b) Per-site callee.** The three routes check out (bytecode id rewrite, IR pass, PTX text). The direct_helpers precedent is really per map, not per site. A fourth route exists: free helper argument slots (r5 of update, r3-r5 of lookup/delete) could carry a site id without a new callee. memcapture shifts eBPF pcs and compiles the program once per memory access.
- **(c) Loader reads.** They run in the loader process directly on the segment. No flush channel to the agent exists. The watcher would serve a flag1 posted by another process within about 1 ms, but only GPU atomics guard the slot, so that is not a usable channel.
- **(d) Hash value pointers.** fix_size is the only compiled hash map. A value pointer follows the element: an ANY/EXIST update retires it as the stripe's spare, and a delete frees it. Hash storage is never pinned, and a loader close frees it.
- **(e) Auto-warp.** The rules match the code. The += admission holds by reading: `*val = *val + 1` with a uniform key is admitted, and leader-only runs count once per converged group. That undercounts against a per-thread count but equals today's lockstep collapse. Dev lacks #740.
- **(f) Hooks and flush points.** Only launch, graph-node, registration, cuLibraryLoadData and symbol-memcpy calls are hooked; nothing on synchronize, memcpy or graph launch. CUDA 13 handle launches hit the hook but are not noted. Completion is known only through per-stream event polling.

**Contradictions resolved:**
- Passes are loaded with dlmopen, not dlopen.
- The build uses LLVM 15, not 16.
- activemask is fine at sm_61; only LLVM-lowered sm_70+ intrinsics are limited.
- The request slot is per segment, not per process.
- Per-CPU host calls take the userspace path (CPU 0's value or NULL), not the watcher's CPU.
- The pass thread pool runs one task per PTX file, not per (entry, kernel).
- The host-call set is wider than the task text says.
- The timestamp idiom's deletes use a constant key, not a per-block one.

**Main remaining unknowns:** atomic scope and CPU visibility on registered memory, O3 call-site merging, and whether warp intrinsics written as PTX text are accepted after the retarget.
